Average speeds in EPA MOVES are intended to be representative of the average speed of driving cycles that are currently greater than 4 minutes in length and classified by day type (weekend or weekday), hour of the day, road type, and vehicle type. For the segments, the data are grouped by date to ensure that segments meant to represent driving cycle average speeds were not aggregated across separate dates. When we examine averages and distributions in the following analyses, the date column will be dropped upon grouping. 7 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Once grouped on the day type, hour type, road type, vehicle type, and date, the average speed data for each 10-second to 2-minute segment are stored in a folder named linkResultsByVid with a separate .csv file for each vehicle. The .csv files are named, for example, “two_min_segments_comb_short_haul_132.csv,” or, more generally, “two_min_segments_source_type_vehicleID.csv.” 8 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 4 Data Density We discuss the data density for the FleetDNA and CE-CERT data sets to demonstrate how combining their data can augment data coverage in certain categories. We depict both vehicle counts and hours of data recorded per each category of source type, road type, day type, and hour of the day. Vehicle count and driving time were utilized from results and data files in Section 5.3: Average Speed. Drilling down to this temporal and spatial resolution can make certain categories of data too sparse to continue reporting or necessitate that results be examined with caution in some cases. We also note that while some individual vehicles show diversity in their day-to-day driving, other vehicles may perform the same route day after day; this repetition may generate hours of data for a given source type or vocation while underrepresenting the group as a whole. The greater number of vehicles and greater unique fleets that compose a category, the more likely the full activity usage of the source type or vocation is represented. In most cases, we analyze the vehicle count in this section, but for transit buses, we additionally examine fleet count due to lower-than-ideal vehicle count numbers. 4.1 FleetDNA Data Density The FleetDNA data are segmented into many separate categories, namely SourceTypeID, RoadTypeID, DayID, and HourID.
